findings.claim: Every lesson teaches a two-part question: 'part (a)' 20-mark extract analysis plus 'part (b)' 20-mark wider-text response. All 48 practice questions are labelled [20 marks] with 17-20/13-16/9-12/5-8/1-4 band ladders; L8 knowledge checks 2-4 and a flashcard test the split directly.
findings.truth: Section A of the post-1914 prose/drama paper is ONE source-based question worth 40 marks, with an extract printed on the paper. There are no parts and no 20-mark halves. The paper is 2 hours 30 minutes for three 40-mark sections, so the drama question is worth about 50 minutes.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md lines 405-425 (Section A, 40 marks, source based, AO1/AO2/AO4, closed book) and 392-394 (2h30, 60%)

findings.claim: AO4 is defined as 'show understanding of the relationship between texts and the contexts in which they were written' (L1 dfn + glossary, L8 dfn + glossary) and students are told context earns marks: 'AO4 marks are awarded for showing how context shapes meaning' (L1 exam tip), 'Link every point to AO4 context' (L8), 'For AO4, ...' (L3, L6, L8).
findings.truth: That is AO3. Section A assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4 only, and AO4 is 'use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation'. AO3 (context) is NOT assessed on this question, so context earns no marks; it can only support a point about the text.
findings.evidence: specs/eduqas/english-literature-C720QS.md lines 405-425 (Section A, 40 marks, source based, AO1/AO2/AO4, closed book) and 392-394 (2h30, 60%); AO definitions at lines 484-494

findings.claim: 'The Boy is never given a name in the play, which is a deliberate choice by Delaney' - repeated in the key fact, the conclusion, knowledge check 4, three flashcards and the L5 matching answer 'Unnamed tenderness'.
findings.truth: He is named Jimmie in the dialogue. Only Delaney's cast list and speech headings call him 'the Boy'. The reading still works, but the flat claim that he is nameless is false.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/a-taste-of-honey/study-guide/summary-act-one-scene-two ; https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/act-1-scene-2 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Taste_of_Honey ('The Boy/Jimmy')

findings.claim: 'Eduqas' appears in student-facing text in lessons 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8 - 'Understanding this setting is essential for the Eduqas exam', 'Why Context Matters for the Eduqas Exam', 'For the Eduqas exam...', the L8 description and the L8 knowledge checks.
findings.truth: House rule: Eduqas lessons never name the board in student-facing text. Reworded to 'the exam', 'the drama question', 'this section'.
findings.evidence: feedback_eduqas_wjec_neutral_phrasing (house rule)

findings.claim: The unit contradicts itself on Delaney's age: L1 content and L6 say 19, while the L1 description, the L1 conclusion, knowledge check 1 and flashcards in L1 and L6 say 18.
findings.truth: Delaney was born 25 November 1938 and the play opened 27 May 1958, so she was 19 when she wrote it. Sources do vary between 18 and 19; the unit has been standardised on 19, which matches its own prose.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Taste_of_Honey ('written when she was 19'); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelagh_Delaney (b. 25 Nov 1938)

findings.claim: 'The 1958 Notting Hill race riots occurred just a year before the play transferred to the West End' (also a flashcard).
findings.truth: The riots were late August to early September 1958. The play opened 27 May 1958 and transferred to the West End on 10 February 1959, so the riots came a few months AFTER the premiere and about five months before the transfer.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Taste_of_Honey (premiere 27 May 1958; Wyndham's 10 February 1959)

findings.claim: "Jo's first line, 'The roof's leaking'" - stated in the content, the key fact, knowledge check 1 (answer key) and a flashcard.
findings.truth: The play opens HELEN: 'Well! This is the place.' JO: 'And I don't like it.' 'The roof's leaking' is not Jo's first line and could not be found anywhere in the play.
findings.evidence: https://www.studysmarter.co.uk/explanations/english-literature/dramatists/taste-of-honey/ ; https://www.coursehero.com/lit/A-Taste-of-Honey/quotes/ ; absent from the 1958 manuscript at https://archive.org/details/atasteofhoneyw.rededits

findings.claim: 'He is described in the stage directions as wearing a loud check suit and driving a flashy car' (L2); 'His loud check suit and flashy car signal his superficiality' (L5).
findings.truth: Peter is a car salesman who wears a black patch over one eye - that is his stage description, and it is the detail an extract question would turn on. There is no check suit in the play.
findings.evidence: https://stageagent.com/characters/26531/a-taste-of-honey/peter ; https://www.gradesaver.com/a-taste-of-honey/study-guide/summary-act-one-scene-one ; manuscript stage direction 'Over his left eye he wears a black patch'

findings.claim: Jo 'is also realistic, asking "How can you marry me? You're only a sailor."' and 'Jo asks him, "Do you think I'm really beautiful?"'; the ring goes 'on a ribbon around her neck ... suggesting she treasures the relationship but knows it cannot become a conventional marriage'.
findings.truth: Neither quotation could be found in the play or in Delaney's manuscript, and Jo does not question the marriage on those grounds - she accepts. The ring goes on a piece of string because it is too big for her finger; she is still at school and hides it from Helen. The attested line here is the Boy's 'You're the first girl I've met who really didn't care.'
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/a-taste-of-honey/study-guide/summary-act-one-scene-two (ring too big, asks for string); https://www.studysmarter.co.uk/explanations/english-literature/dramatists/taste-of-honey/ (ring on 'a string'; 'first girl I've met who really didn't care'); manuscript Act 1 Sc 2

findings.claim: 'The wedding happens offstage, and Jo is not invited - a detail that underlines her exclusion from Helen's new life.'
findings.truth: Helen raises the idea of Jo being a bridesmaid and Jo waves it away. Jo is not excluded; she excludes herself.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/act-1-scene-2

findings.claim: '"I really do live at the same time as myself, don't I?" captures Jo's self-awareness and the bittersweet innocence of her relationship with the Boy' (conclusion), and a flashcard sites the line 'in Act 1 Scene 2'.
findings.truth: The line belongs to Jo's 'And me, I'm contemporary. I really am, aren't I?' run, which answers Helen's remark that the flat's wallpaper is 'contemporary'. It is not part of the scene with the Boy. The scene reference has been removed rather than reassigned, because sources split between Act 1 Scene 1 and Act 2.
findings.evidence: Full line 'And me, I'm contemporary. I really am, aren't I? I really do live at the same time as myself, don't I?'; Helen's paired line 'there's a lovely view of the gasworks ... and this wallpaper's contemporary' (Act 1 Sc 1) - https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/characters/jo

findings.claim: Knowledge check 2 answer key: 'He joins the navy and sails away.'
findings.truth: The Boy is already a serving sailor, home on leave; he says he finishes with the navy in six months and goes back to sea.
findings.evidence: Manuscript Act 1 Sc 2, 'I finish with the navy in six months, Jo'; https://www.gradesaver.com/a-taste-of-honey/study-guide/summary-act-one-scene-two

findings.claim: Flashcard: 'Who is the Windrush generation that the Boy belongs to?'
findings.truth: The Boy explicitly says his family are not recent arrivals from Africa or the Caribbean - they come from Cardiff. He is not of the Windrush generation. The Windrush background is fair general context for 1950s racial attitudes, but it cannot be attached to him.
findings.evidence: Manuscript Act 1 Sc 2: 'From darkest Africa? No - at least not my immediate ancestors - we come from Cardiff.'

findings.claim: 'Helen and Peter later weaponise Geof's sexuality against him, calling him a "pansified little freak"' (L4); 'They call him a "little freak"' (L8).
findings.truth: 'Pansified little freak' is Helen's phrase for Geof. Peter's insults are different ones.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/a-taste-of-honey/act-2-scene-1 (Helen uses the term of Geoffrey when speaking to Jo)

findings.claim: Flashcard L4: 'Which short Jo quote sums up the pregnancy's reality?' -> 'The dream has gone but the baby is real.' Flashcard L5: 'Which short Jo line quotes the Boy on her baby's reality?'
findings.truth: The line is Geof's, spoken to Jo late in the play. It is not Jo's, and it is not a quotation of the Boy.
findings.evidence: Widely cited as Geoffrey's line to Jo - the source of The Smiths' 'This Night Has Opened My Eyes'; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Taste_of_Honey

findings.claim: 'The entire play takes place in one location: a rented flat in Salford' (also knowledge check 3 and a flashcard).
findings.truth: Delaney's opening stage direction is 'The stage represents a comfortless flat in Manchester and the street outside.' It is one unchanging set, but it holds two playing areas, and the street is used - Act 1 Scene 2 opens with Jo and the Boy under the street lamp.
findings.evidence: https://studyrocket.co.uk/revision/gcse-drama-aqa/a-taste-of-honey/a-taste-of-honey-stage-directions ; manuscript 'Scene. a section of a street and a flat.'

findings.claim: Practice question 1: 'Read the passage where Jo tells Geof "I'm not just talented, I'm geniused."'
findings.truth: Jo says it to Helen in Act 1 Scene 1, replying to Helen's remark about her drawings. Geof does not appear until Act 2.
findings.evidence: https://www.thestudentroom.co.uk/g/revision-tests/a-taste-of-honey-quotes-act-one-scene-one (Act One Scene One, reply to Helen); manuscript line 160

findings.claim: Seven quotations carry a lot of weight in this unit and could not be found in any study guide, quotation list, or Delaney's 1958 manuscript: 'We're all out of the same cup' (L2, L5, L7, L8 - three knowledge checks and three flashcards), Jo's reply 'Yes, and it's a very dirty cup' (staged as a verbatim exchange in L7), 'Oh well, it's a lovely morning for it' (L2, L4, L5, L7), 'that ugly-looking thing' (L2 content + answer key), 'Are you really a homosexual?' (L4, L7 + a practice question and a flashcard), 'You're just a selfish old woman' (L7), 'I'd sooner be more to you than that' (L4, L7), and Helen calling Jo 'useless' (L3).
findings.truth: Two options. (a) They are genuine lines that the online guides simply do not index, in which case nothing needs doing. (b) They are fabricated, in which case they are the largest problem in the unit, because students are being told to memorise them for a closed-book exam. I could not settle it without a copy of the Methuen text. Recommendation: check the seven strings against a printed copy; anything absent should be replaced with an attested line, and the three knowledge checks and three flashcards built on 'the same cup' rebuilt. Related: L4 claims 'Oh well, it's a lovely morning for it' resurfaces in Act 2, which is a second, structural claim resting on the same unverified line.
findings.evidence: Absent from LitCharts, GradeSaver, Course Hero, StudySmarter and Revision World quotation lists, and from https://archive.org/details/atasteofhoneyw.rededits (Delaney's 1958 manuscript, grepped)

findings.claim: L1 content says kitchen sink drama rejected 'upper-class theatre'; the L1 flashcard and L7 say 'middle-class'.
findings.truth: Both descriptions are commonly used and neither is wrong. Left alone.

findings.claim: Delaney's opening stage direction names Manchester, while the unit says Salford throughout.
findings.truth: Salford is the universal reading (Delaney's own city, and Wikipedia and every guide locate the play there). Left as Salford; worth knowing if a student quotes the stage direction.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Taste_of_Honey ('set in Salford'); stage direction 'a comfortless flat in Manchester'

findings.claim: The unit never mentions that the Boy's family come from Cardiff, nor that he was a male nurse before national service.
findings.truth: Both are in the text and both complicate the 'Windrush' framing. Not errors, just gaps worth a future top-up.
findings.evidence: Manuscript Act 1 Sc 2 ('we come from Cardiff'); Act 2 ('He was a male nurse in the navy')

summary: All 8 lessons carry findings. The unit teaches an invented exam format (a two-part 20+20 question) and defines AO4 as context, telling students context earns marks when this section assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4 only and gives no credit for AO3; 219 edits correct that plus Jo's opening line, the claim that the Boy is nameless, Peter's stage description, the speaker of 'The dream has gone but the baby is real', the Windrush attribution and the board naming. One ADJUDICATE: seven load-bearing quotations could not be verified in any source or in Delaney's 1958 manuscript.
